stages.title: Intermediate vocabulary
stages.hook: Russian builds many words from small parts. If учитель is a teacher, what could писатель be?
explain: Many Russian words are made from a root and a suffix. The ending -тель often names a person who does something: учить (to teach) gives учитель, писать (to write) gives писатель (writer). The suffix -ник names a person or thing connected with something: праздник (holiday) from the older word for "free day".
Beware of false friends. Магазин is a shop, not a magazine, and фамилия is a surname, not a family. Learn words in families: здоровье (health), здоровый (healthy), здравствуйте (a wish for health).
stages.mnemonic: Root plus suffix: пис- plus -атель makes a writer.

gq.why: The suffix -тель names a person who does the action: писать, писатель.

gq.q: A Russian says "Это моя фамилия". What does she mean?
gq.why: Фамилия is a false friend: it means surname.

panel.q: Why is it useful to learn words in word families?
o: Families are always spelled the same
Related words share a root, so one word helps with several others
Every word has a unique root
panel.why: Roots such as здоров- appear in several words.

panel.q: What does the word магазин teach us about borrowed words?
o: They keep exactly the same meaning
panel.why: Магазин means shop although it looks like "magazine".

panel.q: Which suffix in the word учитель tells us it is a person who does something?
panel.why: The suffix -тель forms agent nouns.

teach.model: Russian words come from a root and suffixes, so you can guess related words. The suffix -тель names a person who acts, like учитель and писатель. Watch out for false friends such as магазин.

trip.prompt: Find a list of suffixes and make two new words from familiar roots.

stages.title: Verb forms and time expressions
stages.hook: In Russian the past tense of a verb changes with the gender of the speaker. Would a girl say читал or читала?
explain: The past tense uses -л with an ending that matches the subject: он читал, она читала, оно читало, они читали. A girl says Я читала and a boy says Я читал.

The future of the imperfective is formed with будет and the infinitive: я буду читать, ты будешь читать. Time words help: вчера (yesterday), сегодня (today), завтра (tomorrow), всегда (always), иногда (sometimes), никогда не (never), часто (often), уже (already).
stages.mnemonic: Past = -л, plus a gender ending: читал, читала.

gq.q: A girl says "I read" in the past tense. Which form?
How do you say "I will read" (imperfective)?
gq.why: The future uses буду plus an infinitive.

panel.q: Why does the Russian past tense show gender but not person?
o: Past forms come from an old participle that agrees with the subject
panel.why: Он читал, она читала: gender and number, not person.

panel.q: Why is "Она никогда не опаздывает" correct with two negatives?
o: It means she is often late, so two negatives cancel
Russian uses a negative word together with не
panel.why: Double negation is the rule.

panel.q: What does уже add in Я уже читал?
o: Already: the action is completed before now
panel.why: Уже means "already".

teach.model: The past tense ends in -л and shows gender: читал, читала, читало, читали. The future of an imperfective verb is буду plus an infinitive. Use time words like вчера, завтра, всегда and никогда не.

points.ask: How do I make the past?
How do I make the future?

trip.prompt: Find the page about the past tense and compare the four forms of one verb.

stages.title: Complex sentence introduction
stages.hook: English says "If it rains, we stay home" with a present verb. Which tense does Russian use?
explain: A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause. Always put a comma between them: Я знаю, что ты прав. Common words: что (that), который (which, who), если (if), когда (when), хотя (although), чтобы (in order to), пока (while).

Russian says Если будет дождь, мы останемся дома: it uses the future in the if-clause because the rain has not happened yet. The word который agrees with its noun in gender and number: Это девочка, которая живёт рядом.
stages.mnemonic: Every extra clause meets a comma.
sentences: I know that you are right.
If it rains, we will stay at home.
I learn Russian in order to read books.

gq.q: Where is the comma in this sentence?
gq.why: A comma goes before что when it joins two clauses.

gq.q: Which tense follows если when rain is still uncertain?
o: Present only: если идёт дождь always
gq.why: Russian uses the future for a future condition.

panel.q: Why is it девочка, которая, but мальчик, который?
o: It agrees with the verb only
Который agrees in gender with the noun it describes
panel.why: Который, которая, которое follow the noun.

panel.q: What does чтобы express in Я учу русский, чтобы читать книги?
panel.why: Чтобы means "in order to".

panel.q: Which word shows contrast: Хотя было холодно, мы гуляли?
panel.why: Хотя means although.

teach.model: Join clauses with что, который, если, когда, хотя and чтобы and put a comma between clauses. Который agrees with the noun in gender. After если, use the future when the event has not happened yet.

points.ask: How do I make an if sentence?

trip.prompt: Find an example of the word который and underline the noun it refers to.

stages.title: Reading short stories
stages.hook: Many Russian fairy tales begin with the words "Жили-были". What do you think they mean?
explain: Russian folk tales (сказки) often start with Жили-были, "once upon a time there lived". Famous characters are Колобок, a round bun that escapes and meets animals, Баба-яга and animals such as волк (wolf), медведь (bear) and лиса (fox).

Stories use the past tense. Imperfective verbs describe background and repeated events: Лиса жила в лесу. Perfective verbs show completed events. Many tales end with a rhymed ending, and small endings such as -ок (колобок) make a warm tone. The great poet Pushkin also wrote fairy tales in verse.
stages.mnemonic: Жили-были opens the door, and the story walks in.
items: once upon a time there lived
sentences: Once there lived an old bear.
A fox lived in the forest.
This is the end of the tale.

gq.q: How do many Russian fairy tales begin?
gq.why: This formula is the Russian "once upon a time".

gq.q: Who tricks the bun in the tale Колобок?
gq.why: The fox flatters the bun and eats it at the end.

panel.q: Why is a small ending like -ок used in колобок?
o: Diminutives give a friendly, small feeling
panel.why: Diminutive suffixes are common in tales and speech.

panel.q: In a story the sentence Лиса жила в лесу uses an imperfective verb. Why?
o: It describes a state that lasted, background to the story
panel.why: Imperfective verbs describe ongoing or background situations.

panel.q: Which Russian poet wrote tales in verse?
panel.why: Pushkin wrote verse fairy tales, such as The Tale of the Fisherman and the Fish.

teach.model: Russian tales start with Жили-были and use the past tense. Characters include the fox, wolf and bear and Колобок. Diminutive endings like -ок give a warm tone.

trip.prompt: Read the summary and tell the story in three steps.

stages.title: Listening comprehension
stages.hook: You hear Russian and catch only half of the words. What helps you understand?
explain: Two verbs mean hear: слышать is to hear without effort, and слушать is to listen on purpose. Я слышу музыку means "I hear music", while Я слушаю музыку means "I am listening to music".

Spoken Russian differs from spelling: что is said "shto", его is said "yevo" and сегодня is said "sevodnya". Speakers also swallow unstressed vowels. Listen for stress and intonation first, and guess the general meaning from key words.
stages.mnemonic: Слышать happens to you, слушать you do.
sentences: I hear but do not understand.

gq.q: Which verb means to listen on purpose?

gq.why: In что (and чтобы) the letters чт are said "sht", although чт is usually "cht" in other words such as чтение.

panel.q: Why can spelling be a poor guide to listening?
o: Russian has no fixed spelling system at all, so words vary
Spoken Russian reduces vowels and changes some sounds
Speakers read aloud letter by letter
panel.why: Reduction and special readings mean sound differs from letters.

panel.q: A friend says "его" quickly. What do you hear?
panel.why: The г in the ending -ого/-его is pronounced like в.

panel.q: What is a good strategy for understanding fast speech?
o: Translate every word into English as you listen
Stop at the first new word
Listen for stress and key words first
panel.why: Meaning can be built from stressed key words.

teach.model: Слышать is to hear and слушать is to listen on purpose. Spoken Russian differs from spelling, so что sounds like "shto". Listen for stress and key words.

points.ask: What is the difference between hear and listen?
How can I follow fast speech?

trip.prompt: Find a list of pronunciation differences and read two examples aloud.

stages.title: Conversation and pronunciation
stages.hook: The Russian letter ы has no English twin. How do you make this sound?
explain: Practise two tricky sounds. The letter ы is made with the tongue pulled back, like a very short "ih" sound, as in мы (we). It never starts a normal Russian word. Soft consonants are said with the tongue raised to the palate: брать (to take) is not брат (brother).
Intonation matters too. A statement falls at the end, while a question rises on the key word. Make mistakes freely. A common phrase is Повторяй за мной (repeat after me).
stages.mnemonic: Hard and soft: брат ends hard, брать ends soft.
sentences: Do not be afraid of mistakes.

gq.q: What is the difference between брат and брать?
o: The vowel in брать is longer
The final consonant is hard in брат and soft in брать
Брать is the question form of брат
gq.why: The soft sign ь shows a soft consonant.

gq.q: Which letter has no English twin and is made with the tongue pulled back?
gq.why: Ы is a back, short vowel.

panel.q: Why does the soft sign matter in meaning?
o: It can distinguish otherwise identical words
panel.why: Брат and брать differ only by softness.

panel.q: Why practise with a speaker or recording rather than only reading?
o: Intonation and sounds are learned by hearing and imitating
panel.why: Imitation trains the ear and mouth.

panel.q: Which attitude helps pronunciation?
o: Repeating phrases aloud and accepting mistakes
Never speaking until you are completely perfect
panel.why: Speaking practice, even with errors, builds fluency.

teach.model: Ы is a short back vowel. Consonants can be hard or soft, like брат and брать. Intonation falls in a statement and rises in a yes/no question. Practise by repeating aloud.

points.ask: What are hard and soft consonants?

trip.prompt: Find the soft and hard consonants table and read two word pairs.

stages.title: Writing paragraphs
stages.hook: How do you join sentences so that a paragraph tells a clear story from start to finish?
explain: A paragraph begins with an indented first line, called красная строка. Use linking words in order: сначала (first), потом (then), после этого (after that), затем (next), наконец (finally). Add ideas with кроме того (besides) and give examples with например.
Introductory words such as например and наконец are set off by commas. A short paragraph about your day could say: Сначала я завтракаю, потом иду в школу. Наконец, я возвращаюсь домой.
stages.mnemonic: Сначала, потом, наконец: first, then, finally.
sentences: First I read, then I write.

gq.q: What is the Russian name for the indented first line of a paragraph?
gq.why: Красная строка means "red line", the paragraph indent.

gq.q: Which word is set off by a comma?
gq.why: Introductory words are separated by commas.

panel.q: What is the purpose of words like сначала and потом?
o: They change the tense of the whole paragraph
They put ideas in order for the reader
panel.why: Sequencing words guide the reader.

panel.q: A good paragraph has one main idea. How do you check it?
o: Every sentence supports the opening idea
Each sentence starts a completely new topic
panel.why: Paragraph unity makes writing clear.

panel.q: Which version is correct?
panel.why: A comma follows the introductory word наконец.

teach.model: Start with an indent, use sequencing words like сначала, потом and наконец, and set introductory words off with commas. Keep one main idea in the paragraph.

points.ask: How do I put ideas in order?

trip.prompt: Read an example paragraph and underline the linking words.

stages.title: Cultural expressions and idioms
stages.hook: In Russia, people say "No fluff, no feather!" before an exam. What do they mean?
explain: Ни пуха ни пера! comes from hunting and means "Good luck!". Russians traditionally answer К чёрту!, a joking reply, to avoid bad luck, and do not say thank you. Use it among friends.

Idioms cannot be translated word for word. Как рыба в воде ("like a fish in water") means at ease. Лучше поздно, чем никогда means better late than never. Семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь ("measure seven times, cut once") advises care before acting.
stages.mnemonic: Fish in water: nothing is more at home.
items: at ease, like a fish in water
Семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь
Two heads are better than one.
Одна голова хорошо, а две лучше
ad-NA ga-la-VA kha-ra-SHO, a dvye LOOCH-she

gq.q: What do you say to a friend before an exam?
gq.why: This is the traditional good-luck phrase.

gq.q: What does "как рыба в воде" describe?
gq.why: It is an idiom for feeling completely comfortable.

panel.q: Why should idioms not be translated word for word?
o: Their meaning is not the sum of their words
They have no real words, only sounds and gestures
panel.why: An idiom is a fixed expression with its own meaning.

panel.q: What advice does "Семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь" give?
panel.why: It teaches caution and careful preparation.

panel.q: Why do Russians avoid answering Ни пуха ни пера with thanks?
o: Thanks is considered very rude between friends
Tradition says thanks would spoil the luck
They do not know the word
panel.why: The reply К чёрту is traditional and playful.

teach.model: Idioms are fixed expressions with their own meaning, like как рыба в воде for being at ease and Лучше поздно, чем никогда. Say Ни пуха ни пера! to wish luck.

trip.prompt: Pick one proverb from the page and explain its meaning in your own words.

stages.title: Practical travel communication
stages.hook: You arrive at a Russian railway station. Which three words help you most?
explain: Travel words are вокзал (railway station), аэропорт (airport), билет (ticket), паспорт (passport), гостиница (hotel), номер (room), карта (map) and остановка (stop). Signs use Cyrillic: Вход (entrance), Выход (exit), Метро, Касса (ticket office).
To ask for directions say Где находится вокзал? or Как доехать до гостиницы? After до (to, as far as) use the genitive: до вокзала, до Москвы. Buy a ticket with Один билет до Москвы, пожалуйста.
stages.mnemonic: Вход begins with В- (in), выход begins with вы- (out).
sentences: How do I get to the hotel?

gq.q: What does the sign Выход mean?
gq.why: Выход means exit and Вход means entrance.

panel.q: Why is it useful to learn Cyrillic signs before travelling?
o: All signs in Russia are also in English
Many signs have no Latin letters
panel.why: Reading signs helps you move around.

panel.q: You do not understand an answer about directions. What is a polite follow-up?
panel.why: It asks the person to repeat more slowly.

panel.q: Why is it "до гостиницы" and not "до гостиница"?
o: Гостиница is plural, so it must change
The preposition до needs the genitive
panel.why: Every preposition governs a case; до governs the genitive.

teach.model: Learn travel words: вокзал, билет, паспорт and гостиница, and signs like Вход and Выход. Ask Где находится...? and Как доехать до...? Use the genitive after до.

points.ask: How do I ask for directions?

trip.prompt: Look at the station signs and read three names aloud.
